docs.title: listnun documentation
docs.text:
listnun is a newsletter and mailing list platform. You keep your subscribers in lists, write campaigns, send them, and see who opened and clicked. Developers can also send one-off transactional emails, such as receipts and password resets, through an API.

These docs are in three parts. Start with the one that fits you.

  • Using listnun

    For anyone working in a workspace: building lists, importing subscribers, writing and sending campaigns, and reading the results.

    Quickstart: send your first campaign

  • Developers

    For connecting your own systems: API keys, the REST API, transactional email, webhooks and template syntax.

    Developers overview

  • Running listnun

    For people hosting listnun: installation, configuration, upgrades, workspaces and storage.

    Installation

docs.title: Words you'll see
docs.text:
Term Meaning Workspace Your own space in listnun, with its own subscribers, campaigns, team and settings. It has its own address, like yourcompany.listnun.app. List A group of subscribers you send to. A subscriber can be on many lists. Subscriber One person: an email address, a name, and any extra details you keep about them (attributes). Campaign An email you send to one or more lists. Template The layout a campaign sits in: header, footer and styling. Transactional email A single email sent to one person when something happens, such as an order receipt. Sent through the API, not as a campaign.

See Concepts for the details behind each of these.

listnun is built on listmonk, the open-source newsletter manager, and keeps its templating language and most of its API. The source is on GitHub; see Developer setup to work on it.

docs.title: Archives
docs.text:
A global public archive is maintained on the public web interface. It can be enabled under Settings › General › Enable public mailing list archive.

To make a campaign available in the public archive (provided it has been enabled in the settings as described above), enable the option 'Publish to public archive' under Campaigns -> Create new -> Archive.

When using template variables that depend on subscriber data (such as any template variable referencing .Subscriber), such data must be supplied as 'Campaign metadata', which is a JSON object that will be used in place of .Subscriber when rendering the archive template and content.

When individual subscriber tracking is enabled, TrackLink requires that a UUID of an existing user is provided as part of the campaign metadata. Any clicks on a TrackLink from the archived campaign will be counted towards that subscriber.

As an example:

{
  "UUID": "5a837423-a186-5623-9a87-82691cbe3631",
  "email": "example@example.com",
  "name": "Reader",
  "attribs": {}
}

docs.title: Bounce processing
docs.text: Enable bounce processing in Settings › Bounces. POP3 bounce scanning and APIs only become available once the setting is enabled.

docs.title: POP3 bounce mailbox
docs.text:
Configure the bounce mailbox in Settings › Bounces. Either the "From" e-mail that is set on a campaign (or in settings) should have a POP3 mailbox behind it to receive bounce e-mails, or you should configure a dedicated POP3 mailbox and add that address as the Return-Path (envelope sender) header in Settings › SMTP › Custom headers box. For example:

[
    {"Return-Path": "your-bounce-inbox@site.com"}
]

Some mail servers may also return the bounce to the Reply-To address, which can also be added to the header settings.

Warning

Do not use a primary POP3 inbox as the bounce mailbox. Create a dedicated mailbox specifically for bounces. listnun downloads e-mails in the configured mailbox and deletes them from the mailbox after processing.

docs.title: Bounce classification
docs.text: listnun applies a series of heuristics looking for keywords in the bounced mail body to guess if it is a 'soft' bounce or a 'hard' bounce. For instance, 4.x.x and 5.x.x error status codes, common strings such as "mailbox not found" etc. If none of the heuristics match, then the bounce mail is considered to be 'soft' by default.

docs.title: Webhook API
docs.text:
The bounce webhook API can be used to record bounce events with custom scripting. This could be by reading a mailbox, a database, or mail server logs.

Method Endpoint Description POST /webhooks/bounce Record a bounce event. Name Type Required Description subscriber_uuid string The UUID of the subscriber. Either this or email is required. email string The e-mail of the subscriber. Either this or subscriber_uuid is required. campaign_uuid string UUID of the campaign for which the bounce happened. source string Yes A string indicating the source, eg: api, my_script etc. type string Yes hard or soft bounce. Currently, this has no effect on how the bounce is treated. meta string An optional escaped JSON string with arbitrary metadata about the bounce event. 
curl -u 'api_username:access_token' -X POST 'http://localhost:9000/webhooks/bounce' \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{"email": "user1@mail.com", "campaign_uuid": "9f86b50d-5711-41c8-ab03-bc91c43d711b", "source": "api", "type": "hard", "meta": "{\"additional\": \"info\"}}'

docs.title: External webhooks
docs.text:
listnun supports receiving bounce webhook events from the following SMTP providers.

Endpoint Description More info https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/ses Amazon (AWS) SES See below https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/azure Azure Communication Services (ACS) More info https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/sendgrid Sendgrid / Twilio Signed event webhook More info https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/postmark Postmark webhook More info https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/forwardemail Forward Email webhook More info https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/lettermint Lettermint webhook More info

docs.title: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
docs.text:
If using SES as your SMTP provider, automatic bounce processing is the recommended way to maintain your sender reputation. The settings below are based on Amazon's recommendations. Please note that your sending domain must be verified in SES before proceeding.

  1. In listnun settings, go to the "Bounces" tab and configure the following:
    • Enable bounce processing: Enabled
      • Soft:
        • Bounce count: 2
        • Action: None
      • Hard:
        • Bounce count: 1
        • Action: Blocklist
      • Complaint:
        • Bounce count: 1
        • Action: Blocklist
    • Enable bounce webhooks: Enabled
    • Enable SES: Enabled
  2. In the AWS console, go to Simple Notification Service and create a new topic with the following settings:
    • Type: Standard
    • Name: ses-bounces (or any other name)
  3. Create a new subscription to that topic with the following settings:
    • Protocol: HTTPS
    • Endpoint: https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/ses
    • Enable raw message delivery: Disabled (unchecked)
  4. SES will then make a request to your listnun instance to confirm the subscription. After a page refresh, the subscription should have a status of "Confirmed". If not, your endpoint may be incorrect or not publicly accessible.
  5. In the AWS console, go to Simple Email Service and click "Identities" in the left sidebar.
  6. Click your domain and go to the "Notifications" tab.
  7. Next to "Feedback notifications", click "Edit".
  8. For both "Bounce feedback" and "Complaint feedback", use the following settings:
    • SNS topic: ses-bounces (or whatever you named it)
    • Include original email headers: Enabled (checked)
  9. Repeat steps 6-8 for any Email address identities you send from using listnun
  10. Bounce processing should now be working. You can test it with SES simulator addresses. Add them as subscribers, send them campaign previews, and ensure that the appropriate action was taken after the configured bounce count was reached.
    • Soft bounce: ooto@simulator.amazonses.com
    • Hard bounce: bounce@simulator.amazonses.com
    • Complaint: complaint@simulator.amazonses.com
  11. You can optionally disable email feedback forwarding.

docs.title: Azure Communication Services (ACS)
docs.text:
If you use Azure Communication Services Email, listnun can receive delivery report events from Azure Event Grid and turn them into bounces.

  1. In listnun settings, go to "Bounces" and configure:
    • Enable bounce processing: Enabled
    • Enable bounce webhooks: Enabled
    • Enable Azure ACS: Enabled
    • Optional: set Azure Event Grid Shared Secret.
    • Optional: set Azure Shared Secret Header Name if you want listnun to read the secret from a header (defaults to X-Listnun-Webhook-Secret).
  2. In listnun settings, go to "SMTP" and use the Azure ACS quick preset to fill SMTP defaults.
  3. In Azure, create an Event Grid subscription for your ACS Email events with:
    • Endpoint type: Web Hook
    • Endpoint URL: https://listnun.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/azure
    • If using query-param auth, append ?code=<your-shared-secret>.
    • If using header auth, configure Event Grid to include the same secret in the header name configured in listnun.
  4. During subscription creation, Event Grid sends a subscription validation event. listnun automatically returns validationResponse for this handshake.
  5. Subscribe to Microsoft.Communication.EmailDeliveryReportReceived events. listnun maps relevant statuses to bounce records.
  6. Send test mail and verify bounces in listnun.

docs.title: Exporting bounces
docs.text:
Bounces can be exported via the JSON API: 

curl -u 'username:passsword' 'http://localhost:9000/api/bounces'

Or by querying the database directly: 

SELECT bounces.created_at,
    bounces.subscriber_id,
    subscribers.uuid AS subscriber_uuid,
    subscribers.email AS email
FROM bounces
LEFT JOIN subscribers ON (subscribers.id = bounces.subscriber_id)
ORDER BY bounces.created_at DESC LIMIT 1000;

docs.title: Subscriber
docs.text: A subscriber is a recipient identified by an e-mail address and name. Subscribers receive e-mails that are sent from listnun. A subscriber can be added to any number of lists. Subscribers who are not a part of any lists are considered orphan records.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attributes are arbitrary properties attached to a subscriber in addition to their e-mail and name. They are represented as a JSON map. It is not necessary for all subscribers to have the same attributes. Subscribers can be queried and segmented into lists based on their attributes, and the attributes can be inserted into the e-mails sent to them. For example:

{
  "city": "Bengaluru",
  "likes_tea": true,
  "spoken_languages": ["English", "Malayalam"],
  "projects": 3,
  "stack": {
    "frameworks": ["echo", "go"],
    "languages": ["go", "python"],
    "preferred_language": "go"
  }
}

docs.title: Subscription statuses
docs.text:
A subscriber can be added to one or more lists, and each such relationship can have one of these statuses.

Status Description unconfirmed The subscriber was added to the list directly without their explicit confirmation. Nonetheless, the subscriber will receive campaign messages sent to single opt-in campaigns. confirmed The subscriber confirmed their subscription by clicking on 'accept' in the confirmation e-mail. Only confirmed subscribers in opt-in lists will receive campaign messages send to the list. unsubscribed The subscriber is unsubscribed from the list and will not receive any campaign messages sent to the list.

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text: Segmentation is the process of filtering a large list of subscribers into a smaller group based on arbitrary conditions, primarily based on their attributes. For instance, if an e-mail needs to be sent subscribers who live in a particular city, given their city is described in their attributes, it's possible to quickly filter them out into a new list and e-mail them. Learn more.

docs.title: List
docs.text: A list (or a mailing list) is a collection of subscribers grouped under a name, for instance, clients. Lists are used to organise subscribers and send e-mails to specific groups. A list can be single opt-in or double opt-in. Subscribers added to double opt-in lists have to explicitly accept the subscription by clicking on the confirmation e-mail they receive. Until then, they do not receive campaign messages.

docs.title: Campaign
docs.text: A campaign is an e-mail (or any other kind of messages) that is sent to one or more lists.

docs.title: Transactional message
docs.text: A transactional message is an arbitrary message sent to a subscriber using the transactional message API. For example a welcome e-mail on signing up to a service; an order confirmation e-mail on purchasing an item; a password reset e-mail when a user initiates an online account recovery process.

docs.title: Template
docs.text: A template is a re-usable HTML design that can be used across campaigns and when sending arbitrary transactional messages. Most commonly, templates have standard header and footer areas with logos and branding elements, where campaign content is inserted in the middle. listnun supports Go template expressions that lets you create powerful, dynamic HTML templates. Learn more.

docs.title: Messenger
docs.text: listnun supports multiple custom messaging backends in additional to the default SMTP e-mail backend, enabling not just e-mail campaigns, but arbitrary message campaigns such as SMS, FCM notifications etc. A Messenger is a web service that accepts a campaign message pushed to it as a JSON request, which the service can in turn broadcast as SMS, FCM etc. Learn more.

docs.title: Tracking pixel
docs.text: The tracking pixel is a tiny, invisible image that is inserted into an e-mail body to track e-mail views. This allows measuring the read rate of e-mails. While this is exceedingly common in e-mail campaigns, it carries privacy implications and should be used in compliance with rules and regulations such as GDPR. It is possible to track reads anonymously without associating an e-mail read to a subscriber. Campaigns can also carry third-party tracking pixels from ad and analytics platforms. See Tracking opens and clicks.

docs.title: Click tracking
docs.text: It is possible to track the clicks on every link that is sent in an e-mail. This allows measuring the clickthrough rates of links in e-mails. While this is exceedingly common in e-mail campaigns, it carries privacy implications and should be used in compliance with rules and regulations such as GDPR. It is possible to track link clicks anonymously without associating an e-mail read to a subscriber. In listnun, one switch on a campaign tracks every link in it. See Tracking opens and clicks.

docs.title: Bounce
docs.text: A bounce occurs when an e-mail that is sent to a recipient "bounces" back for one of many reasons including the recipient address being invalid, their mailbox being full, or the recipient's e-mail service provider marking the e-mail as spam. listnun can automatically process such bounce e-mails that land in a configured POP mailbox, or via APIs of SMTP e-mail providers such as AWS SES and Sengrid. Based on settings, subscribers returning bounced e-mails can either be blocklisted or deleted automatically. Learn more.

docs.title: TOML Configuration file
docs.text:
One or more TOML files can be read by passing --config config.toml multiple times. Apart from a few low level configuration variables and the database configuration, all other settings can be managed from the Settings dashboard on the admin UI.

To generate a new sample configuration file, run listnun --new-config

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variables defined in config.toml can also be provided as environment variables prefixed by LISTNUN_ with periods replaced by __ (double underscore). To start listnun purely with environment variables without a configuration file, set the environment variables and pass the config flag as --config="".

Supported variables:

Environment variable Example value LISTNUN_app__address "0.0.0.0:9000" LISTNUN_db__host db LISTNUN_db__port 9432 LISTNUN_db__user listnun LISTNUN_db__password listnun LISTNUN_db__database listnun LISTNUN_db__ssl_mode disable

docs.title: listnun-specific settings
docs.text:
These are only in the configuration file (or environment), not in the Settings screens.

Setting Default What it does app.multi_tenancy_enabled false Host many workspaces on one instance. See Workspaces and the operator API. app.root_domain With multi-tenancy, workspaces live at <slug>.<root_domain>. app.console_url Where a suspended workspace's admin app redirects (/billing for suspended, the root for disabled). Empty returns a plain 503. app.webhooks_allow_private false Let Developers › Webhooks call plain HTTP and private or loopback addresses. For local development only: on a shared install it lets workspaces reach internal hosts. operator.token Turns on the operator API with this bearer token. Empty keeps it off. operator.db_user, operator.db_password A separate Postgres role with BYPASSRLS for the operator API's cross-workspace reads. operator.env dev adds a -dev suffix to generated workspace hosts, so dev and prod can share a root domain. inactive_cleanup.managed.* 180 days, either, unsubscribe, Sundays 02:00 The rules workspaces get in Inactive cleanup › Managed mode: days (30–3650), activity (opened, clicked or either), action (unsubscribe, blocklist or delete), list_ids (empty for all lists) and schedule (a cron expression). Invalid values fall back to the defaults, with a log line. 
[inactive_cleanup.managed]
days = 180
activity = "either"
action = "unsubscribe"
list_ids = []
schedule = "0 2 * * 0"

docs.title: Customizing system templates
docs.text: See system templates.

docs.title: HTTP routes
docs.text: When configuring auth proxies and web application firewalls, use this table.

docs.title: Private admin endpoints.
docs.text: Methods Route Description * /api/* Admin APIs, the Developers API and the operator API. Your own systems calling the API need this too. GET /admin/* Admin UI and HTML pages POST /webhooks/bounce Admin bounce webhook

docs.title: Using filesystem
docs.text:
When configuring docker volume mounts for using filesystem media uploads, you can follow either of two approaches. The second may be necessary if your setup requires sudo for docker commands. For S3-compatible storage instead, see Media storage.

After making any changes you will need to run sudo docker compose stop ; sudo docker compose up.

And under https://listnun.mysite.com/admin/settings you put /listnun/uploads.

docs.title: Using volumes
docs.text:
Using docker volumes, you can specify the name of volume and destination for the files to be uploaded inside the container.

app:
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: listnun-uploads
        target: /listnun/uploads

volumes:
  listnun-uploads:

Note

This volume is managed by docker itself, and you can see find the host path with docker volume inspect listnun_listnun-uploads.

docs.title: Using bind mounts
docs.text:
app:
    volumes:
      - ./path/on/your/host/:/path/inside/container
Eg: 
  app:
    volumes:
      - ./data/uploads:/listnun/uploads
The files will be available inside /data/uploads directory on the host machine.

To use the default uploads folder: 

  app:
    volumes:
      - ./uploads:/listnun/uploads

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/logs/ 

sudo docker logs -f
sudo docker logs listnun_app -t
sudo docker logs listnun_db -t
sudo docker logs --help
Container info: sudo docker inspect listnun_listnun

Docker logs to /dev/stdout and /dev/stderr. The logs are collected by the docker daemon and stored in your node's host path (by default). The same can be configured (/etc/docker/daemon.json) in your docker daemon settings to setup other logging drivers, logrotate policy and more, which you can read about here.

docs.title: Binary
docs.text:
listnun logs to stdout, which is usually not saved to any file. To save listnun logs to a file use ./listnun > listnun.log.

Settings › Logs in the admin app is each workspace's own activity log (settings changes, campaign and import events, webhook failures), kept in the database for 30 days. It isn't the server log.

For a systemd service, you can use ExecStart=/bin/bash -ce "exec /usr/bin/listnun --config /etc/listnun/config.toml --static-dir /etc/listnun/static >>/etc/listnun/listnun.log 2>&1" to create a log file that persists after restarts. More info.

docs.title: Time zone
docs.text:
To change listnun's time zone (logs, etc.) edit docker-compose.yml: 

environment:
    - TZ=Etc/UTC
with any Timezone listed here. Then run sudo docker-compose stop ; sudo docker-compose up after making changes.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text: Settings › SMTP › Retries denotes the number of times a message that fails at the moment of sending is retried silently using different connections from the SMTP pool. The messages that fail even after retries are the ones that are logged as errors and ignored.

docs.title: SMTP ports
docs.text: Some server hosts block outgoing SMTP ports (25, 465). You may have to contact your host to unblock them before being able to send e-mails. Eg: Hetzner.

docs.title: Batch size
docs.text: The batch size parameter is useful when working with very large lists with millions of subscribers for maximising throughput. It is the number of subscribers that are fetched from the database sequentially in a single cycle (~5 seconds) when a campaign is running. Increasing the batch size uses more memory, but reduces the round trip to the database.

docs.title: Developer setup
docs.text: The app has two distinct components, the Go backend and the VueJS frontend. In the dev environment, both are run independently.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
• go
  • nodejs (if you are working on the frontend) and yarn
  • Postgres database. If there is no local installation, the demo docker DB can be used for development (docker compose up demo-db)

docs.title: First time setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/nerd-zero/listnun.git. The project uses go.mod, so it's best to clone it outside the Go src path.

  1. Copy config.toml.sample as config.toml and add your config.
  2. make dist to build the listnun binary. Once the binary is built, run ./listnun --install to run the DB setup. For subsequent dev runs, use make run.

mailhog is an excellent standalone mock SMTP server (with a UI) for testing and dev.

docs.title: Running the dev environment
docs.text:
You can run your dev environment locally or inside containers.

After setting up the dev environment, you can visit http://localhost:8080.

  1. Locally

    • Run make run to start the listnun dev server on :9000.
    • Run make run-frontend to start the Vue frontend in dev mode using yarn on :8080. All /api/* calls are proxied to the app running on :9000. Refer to the frontend README for an overview on how the frontend is structured.

  2. Inside containers (Using Makefile)

    • Run make init-dev-docker to setup container for db.
    • Run make dev-docker to setup docker container suite.
    • Run make rm-dev-docker to clean up docker container suite.

  3. Inside containers (Using devcontainer)

    • Open repo in vscode, open command palette, and select "Dev Containers: Rebuild and Reopen in Container".

It will set up db, and start frontend/backend for you.

docs.title: Production build
docs.text: Run make dist to build the Go binary, build the Javascript frontend, and embed the static assets producing a single self-contained binary, listnun

docs.title: Integrating with external systems
docs.text: In many environments, a mailing list manager's subscriber database is not run independently but as a part of an existing customer database or a CRM. There are multiple ways of keeping listnun in sync with external systems.

docs.title: Using APIs
docs.text: The subscriber APIs offers several APIs to manipulate the subscribers database, like addition, updation, and deletion. For bulk synchronisation, a CSV can be generated (and optionally zipped) and posted to the import API.

docs.title: Interacting directly with the DB
docs.text: listnun uses tables with simple schemas to represent subscribers (subscribers), lists (lists), and subscriptions (subscriber_lists). It is easy to add, update, and delete subscriber information directly with the database tables for advanced usecases. See the table schemas for more information.

docs.title: Internationalization (i18n)
docs.text: listnun comes available in multiple languages thanks to language packs contributed by volunteers. A language pack is a JSON file with a map of keys and corresponding translations. The bundled languages are in the i18n directory. People can pick their language at the bottom of the sign-in page, and a workspace sets its default under Settings › General.

docs.title: Additional language packs
docs.text:
These additional language packs can be downloaded and passed to listnun with the --i18n-dir flag as described in the next section.

Language Description Deutsch (formal) German language with formal pronouns

docs.title: Customizing languages
docs.text: To customize an existing language or to load a new language, put one or more .json language files in a directory, and pass the directory path to listnun with the--i18n-dir=/path/to/dir flag.

docs.title: Contributing a new language
docs.text: Copy i18n/en.json from the i18n directory, translate the values (keep the keys), set _.code and _.name at the top, and send a pull request adding the file. English is the source: new text is added to en.json first, and other languages fall back to it for anything not yet translated.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
listnun is a single Go binary, with the admin app and static files built in. Its only dependency is PostgreSQL 12 or newer.

Using hosted listnun?

You don't need to install anything: your workspace is ready at its own address. This page is for running listnun yourself.

listnun doesn't publish prebuilt binaries or images yet, so you build it from the source on GitHub.

docs.title: Build the binary
docs.text:
You need Go, Node.js and Yarn.

git clone https://github.com/nerd-zero/listnun.git
cd listnun
make dist

This builds the frontend and the visual email builder, compiles the Go code, and packs everything into one listnun binary.

docs.title: Install with the binary
docs.text:
1. ./listnun --new-config writes a config.toml. Edit at least the [db] section.
  2. ./listnun --install creates the tables in your Postgres database.
  3. ./listnun starts the server. Open http://localhost:9000 to create the first admin user and sign in.

Tip

To create the admin user during installation instead, set: LISTNUN_ADMIN_USER=myuser LISTNUN_ADMIN_PASSWORD=xxxxx ./listnun --install

docs.title: Install with Docker
docs.text:
After make dist, build the image from the repository's Dockerfile, then start it with the repository's docker-compose.yml, which runs listnun and Postgres:

docker build -t listnun/listnun:latest .
docker compose up -d

Open http://localhost:9000 to create the admin user. To set it from the start, run LISTNUN_ADMIN_USER=myuser LISTNUN_ADMIN_PASSWORD=xxxxx docker compose up -d the first time.

On every start the container installs the database if needed, then runs any pending upgrades, then starts listnun.

docs.title: Mounting a config.toml
docs.text:
The compose file configures listnun through LISTNUN_* environment variables. To use a config file instead:

  1. Save a config.toml on the host:

    [app]
address = "0.0.0.0:9000"

[db]
host = "listnun_db" # The Postgres container's name in the compose file.
port = 5432
user = "listnun"
password = "listnun"
database = "listnun"
ssl_mode = "disable"
max_open = 25
max_idle = 25
max_lifetime = "300s"

  2. Mount it in docker-compose.yml:

      app:
    volumes:
    - /path/on/your/host/config.toml:/listnun/config.toml

  3. Point the command: at it:

    command: [sh, -c, "./listnun --install --idempotent --yes --config /listnun/config.toml && ./listnun --upgrade --yes --config /listnun/config.toml && ./listnun --config /listnun/config.toml"]

docs.title: After installing
docs.text:
• Set up email sending under Settings › SMTP.
  • Put listnun behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS, and set Settings › General › Root URL to its public address. Links in emails use it.
  • Keep only the public routes reachable from the internet. See Configuration.
  • To host several workspaces on one instance, see Workspaces and the operator API.
  • For media, see Media storage.

To work on listnun's code, see Developer setup.

docs.title: Messengers
docs.text:
listnun supports multiple custom messaging backends in additional to the default SMTP e-mail backend, enabling not just e-mail campaigns, but arbitrary message campaigns such as SMS, FCM notifications etc.

A Messenger is a web service that accepts a campaign message pushed to it as a JSON request, which the service can in turn broadcast as SMS, FCM etc. Messengers are registered in the Settings -> Messengers UI, and can be selected on individual campaigns.

Messengers support optional BasicAuth authentication. Plain text format for campaign content is ideal for messengers such as SMS and FCM.

When a campaign starts, listnun POSTs messages in the following format to the selected messenger's endpoint. The endpoint should return a 200 OK response in case of a successful request.

The address required to broadcast the message, for instance, a phone number or an FCM ID, is expected to be stored and relayed as subscriber attributes. 

{
    "subject": "Welcome to listnun",
    "body": "The message body",
    "content_type": "plain",
    "recipients": [{
        "uuid": "e44b4135-1e1d-40c5-8a30-0f9a886c2884",
        "email": "anon@example.com",

docs.title: OIDC Single Sign On
docs.text: Listnun supports single sign-on with OIDC (OpenID Connect). Any standards compliant OIDC provider can be configured in Settings › Security -> OIDC

docs.title: User auto-creation

docs.title: Querying and segmenting subscribers
docs.text: listnun allows the writing of partial Postgres SQL expressions to query, filter, and segment subscribers.

docs.title: Database fields
docs.text:
These are the fields in the subscriber database that can be queried.

Field Description subscribers.uuid The randomly generated unique ID of the subscriber subscribers.email E-mail ID of the subscriber subscribers.name Name of the subscriber subscribers.status Status of the subscriber (enabled, disabled, blocklisted) subscribers.attribs Map of arbitrary attributes represented as JSON. Accessed via the -> and ->> Postgres operator. subscribers.created_at Timestamp when the subscriber was first added subscribers.updated_at Timestamp when the subscriber was modified

docs.title: Sample attributes
docs.text:
Here's a sample JSON map of attributes assigned to an imaginary subscriber.

{
  "city": "Bengaluru",
  "likes_tea": true,
  "spoken_languages": ["English", "Malayalam"],
  "projects": 3,
  "stack": {
    "frameworks": ["echo", "go"],
    "languages": ["go", "python"],
    "preferred_language": "go"
  }
}

docs.title: Find a subscriber by e-mail
docs.text:
-- Exact match
subscribers.email = 'some@domain.com'

-- Partial match to find e-mails that end in @domain.com.
subscribers.email LIKE '%@domain.com'

docs.title: Find a subscriber by name
docs.text:
-- Find all subscribers whose name start with John.
subscribers.email LIKE 'John%'

docs.title: Multiple conditions
docs.text:
-- Find all Johns who have been blocklisted.
subscribers.email LIKE 'John%' AND subscribers.status = 'blocklisted'

docs.title: Querying subscribers who viewed the campaign email
docs.text:
-- Find all subscribers who viewed the campaign email.
EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM campaign_views WHERE campaign_views.subscriber_id=subscribers.id AND campaign_views.campaign_id=<put_id_of_campaign>)

docs.title: Querying attributes
docs.text:
-- The ->> operator returns the value as text. Find all subscribers
-- who live in Bengaluru and have done more than 3 projects.
-- Here 'projects' is cast into an integer so that we can apply the
-- numerical operator >
subscribers.attribs->>'city' = 'Bengaluru' AND
    (subscribers.attribs->>'projects')::INT > 3

docs.title: Querying nested attributes
docs.text:
-- Find all blocklisted subscribers who like to drink tea, can code Python
-- and prefer coding Go.
--
-- The -> operator returns the value as a structure. Here, the "languages" field
-- The ? operator checks for the existence of a value in a list.
subscribers.status = 'blocklisted' AND
    (subscribers.attribs->>'likes_tea')::BOOLEAN = true AND
    subscribers.attribs->'stack'->'languages' ? 'python' AND
    subscribers.attribs->'stack'->>'preferred_language' = 'go'

To learn how to write SQL expressions to do advancd querying on JSON attributes, refer to the Postgres JSONB documentation.

docs.title: Roles and permissions
docs.text: listnun users have granular permissions to its features, including per-list permissions. Users can login with a username and password, or via an OIDC (OpenID Connect) handshake if an auth provider is connected. Various permissions can be grouped into "user roles", which can be assigned to users. List-specific permissions can be grouped into "list roles".

docs.title: User roles
docs.text:
A user role is a collection of user related permissions. User roles are attached to user accounts. User roles are managed in Workspace › Users › User roles. The permissions are described below.

Group Permission Description lists lists:get_all Get details of all lists lists:manage_all Create, update, and delete all lists subscribers subscribers:get Get individual subscriber details subscribers:get_all Get all subscribers and their details subscribers:manage Add, update, and delete subscribers subscribers:import Import subscribers from external files subscribers:sql_query Run raw SQL queries on subscriber data.WARNING:This permission allows execution of arbitrary SQL expressions and SQL functions. While it is readonly on the table data, it allows querying of all lists and subscribers directly from the database superceding individual list and subscriber permissions. Raw SQL expressions make it possible to obtain Postgres database configuration and potentially interact with other Postgres system features. Give this permission ONLY to trusted users. Learn more. tx:send Send transactional messages to subscribers campaigns campaigns:get Get and view campaigns belonging to permitted lists campaigns:get_all Get and view campaigns across all lists campaigns:get_analytics Access campaign performance metrics campaigns:manage Create, update, and delete campaigns belonging to permitted lists campaigns:manage_all Create, update, and delete campaigns across all lists campaigns:send Start, schedule, pause, resume, and cancel campaigns. This is independent of manage permissions. This is required to send a campaign, even with campaigns:manage_all bounces bounces:get Get email bounce records bounces:manage Process and handle bounced emails webhooks:post_bounce Receive bounce notifications via webhook media media:get Get uploaded media files media:manage Upload, update, and delete media templates templates:get Get email templates templates:manage Create, update, and delete templates users users:get Get system user accounts users:manage Create, update, and delete user accounts WARNING:This permission allows creation of users with any role, including Super Admin. This permission should only be given to Super Admin level accounts roles:get Get user roles and permissions roles:manage Create and modify user roles settings settings:get Get system settings settings:manage Modify system configuration settings:maintain Perform system maintenance tasks developers apikeys:get See API keys (never their secrets) apikeys:manage Create, rotate, revoke and delete API keys tx:logs Read the transactional message log and sending stats webhooks:get See webhook endpoints and deliveries webhooks:manage Create, change and delete webhook endpoints, reveal and rotate their secrets, and retry deliveries

docs.title: List roles
docs.text: A list role is a collection of permissions assigned per list. Each list can be assigned a view (read) or manage (update) permission. List roles are attached to user accounts. Only the lists defined in a list role is accessible by the user, be it on the admin UI or via API calls. Do note that the lists:get_all and lists:manage_all permissions in user roles override all per-list permissions.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
Code that calls the API uses an API key, not a user account. A key has its own scopes instead of a role, and can only do what its scopes allow.

API users, user accounts of the "API" type, were how older versions did this. They've been turned into API keys. Existing ones keep working and are listed under Workspace › Users › API users, but new ones can't be created.

docs.title: subscribers:sql_query
docs.text:
This permission allowers users to write and execute arbitrary SQL queries on the database. Although it is executed as a read-only transaction disallowing changing of data in the database tables, it allows querying of all lists, subscribers and other data directly from the database superceding individual list and subscriber permissions.

Raw SQL expressions also make it possible to obtain Postgres database configuration and potentially interact with other Postgres system features. Give this permission ONLY to trusted users.

If this permission is being assigned to many users, it is highly recommended that you create a custom Postgres role disallowing any privileged operations. For example:

CREATE ROLE listnun_app WITH
    LOGIN
    PASSWORD '...'
    NOSUPERUSER
    NOCREATEDB
    NOCREATEROLE
    NOREPLICATION;

docs.title: Security reports
docs.text: If you spot a security vulnerability in listnun, please report it via GitHub security advisories.

docs.title: What not to report
docs.text: The below listed scenarios are either not security vulnerabilities or are of acceptable risk. They keep getting reported unfortunately. Please refrain from doing so.

docs.title: SQL injection via subscriber query
docs.text:
The subscribers UI (and APIs) support issuing of arbitrary SQL expressions via a query parameter. While listnun ensures that the queries are executed as readonly and has basic checks for target tables to prevent accidental side-effects, it is not really possible to prevent arbitrary Turing-complete SQL expressions from calling various Postgres functions. Postgres itself does not offer an easy way to allow/disallow specific functions.

That's why this feature is behind a special permission subscribers:sql_query and its risks are clearly documented. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to an admin to allow this permission to trusted users.

docs.title: Stored XSS via SVG
docs.text:
In addition to images, listnun allows uploading of arbitrary file types, .html, .js, .svg, .* and does not transform or modify the files. That means, it is possible to have <script>s and other arbitrary content inside HTML and SVG files. It is not possible for listnun to have special checks or transformations for various file types, and many environments legitimately want SVGs and other filetypes to be uploaded.

In a multi-user scenario, it is possible for an admin to decide what file types to allow (Settings › Media uploads). In an environment where SVG (or any other type) is considered risky, they can simply be disallowed from being uploaded.

docs.title: Stored XSS in campaign HTML
docs.text: listnun is a full-fledged HTML content management system (similar to WordPress). It allows campaign messages to have arbitrary HTML, including <script>s, which is a legitimate use case in many environments. While campaign previews within the admin are iframe-sandboxed, when a campaign is published as a webpage (archive view), it will obviously execute whatever <script> it has. This is expected of a content management and publishing system. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to the admin to give appropriate permissions to trusted users if they deem this undesirable.

docs.title: ReDoS/DoS in templating
docs.text: listnun is a full-fledged HTML content management system (similar to WordPress) which provides the full power of the Go templating language in addition to bundling Sprig functions. This allows executing Turing-complete code within templates where it is possible to write code that does loop-within-loop or memory-allocation code that runs within loops that could cause a DoS. There is no way to prevent this. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to the admin to give appropriate permissions to trusted users if they deem this undesirable.

docs.title: Templating
docs.text:
A template is a re-usable HTML design that can be used across campaigns and transactional messages. Most commonly, templates have standard header and footer areas with logos and branding elements, where campaign content is inserted in the middle.

listnun supports Go template expressions that lets you create powerful, dynamic HTML templates. It also integrates 100+ useful Sprig template functions.

Warning

Sprig template functions are powerful and Turing-complete, allowing programming of complex behaviour in templates. This means that it is also possible to program undesired behaviour, such as overloading memory on the host by concatenating large strings in a loop. Ensure that templating (campaigns, templates) permissions are given only to trusted users.

docs.title: Campaign templates
docs.text: Campaign templates are used in an e-mail campaigns. They are managed under Campaigns › Templates and picked on the Content step of the campaign editor.

docs.title: Transactional templates
docs.text: Transactional templates are used for sending transactional messages through the API. They are managed under Developers › Email templates. See Transactional email.

docs.title: Template expressions
docs.text:
There are several template functions and expressions that can be used in campaign and template bodies. They are written in the form {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, that is, an expression between double curly braces {{ and }}. Template expressions are supported in:

  • Campaign body and alt body
  • Campaign subject
  • Campaign headers
  • Transactional message body and alt body
  • Transactional message subject

docs.title: Subscriber fields
docs.text: Expression Description {{ .Subscriber.UUID }} The randomly generated unique ID of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.Email }} E-mail ID of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.Name }} Name of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }} First name of the subscriber (automatically extracted from the name) {{ .Subscriber.LastName }} Last name of the subscriber (automatically extracted from the name) {{ .Subscriber.Status }} Status of the subscriber (enabled, disabled, blocklisted) {{ .Subscriber.Attribs }} Map of arbitrary attributes. Fields can be accessed with ., eg: .Subscriber.Attribs.city {{ .Subscriber.CreatedAt }} Timestamp when the subscriber was first added {{ .Subscriber.UpdatedAt }} Timestamp when the subscriber was modified

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text: Expression Description {{ .Campaign.UUID }} The randomly generated unique ID of the campaign {{ .Campaign.Name }} Internal name of the campaign {{ .Campaign.Subject }} E-mail subject of the campaign {{ .Campaign.FromEmail }} The e-mail address from which the campaign is being sent

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Description {{ Date "2006-01-01" }} Prints the current datetime for the given format expressed as a Go date layout {{ TrackLink "https://link.com" }} Takes a URL and generates a tracking URL over it. For use in campaign bodies and templates. https://link.com@TrackLink Shorthand for TrackLink. Eg: <a href="https://link.com@TrackLink">Link</a> {{ TrackView }} Inserts a single tracking pixel. Should only be used once, ideally in the template footer. {{ UnsubscribeURL }} Unsubscription and Manage preferences URL. Ideal for use in the template footer. {{ UnsubscribeURL }}?manage=true Direct URL to Manage Preferences page. {{ MessageURL }} URL to view the hosted version of an e-mail message. {{ OptinURL }} URL to the double opt-in confirmation page. {{ Safe "<!-- comment -->" }} Add any HTML code as it is.

docs.title: Sprig functions
docs.text: listnun integrates the Sprig library that offers 100+ utility functions for working with strings, numbers, dates etc. that can be used in templating. Refer to the Sprig documentation for the full list of functions.

docs.title: Example template
docs.text:
The expression {{ template "content" . }} should appear exactly once in every template denoting the spot where an e-mail's content is inserted. Here's a sample HTML e-mail that has a fixed header and footer that inserts the content in the middle.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <style>
      body {
        background: #eee;
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        font-size: 6px;
        color: #111;
      }
      header {
        border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;
        padding-bottom: 30px;
        margin-bottom: 30px;
      }
      .container {
        background: #fff;
        width: 450px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        padding: 30px;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <section class="container">
      <header>
        <!-- This will appear in the header of all e-mails.
             The subscriber's name will be automatically inserted here. //-->
        Hi {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }}!
      </header>

      <!-- This is where the e-mail body will be inserted //-->
      <div class="content">
        {{ template "content" . }}
      </div>

      <footer>
        Copyright 2019. All rights Reserved.
      </footer>

      <!-- The tracking pixel will be inserted here //-->
      {{ TrackView }}
    </section>
  </body>
</html>

Info

For use with plaintext campaigns, create a template with no HTML content and just the placeholder {{ template "content" . }}

docs.title: Example campaign body
docs.text:
Campaign bodies can be composed using the built-in WYSIWYG editor or as raw HTML documents. Assuming that the subscriber has a set of attributes defined, this example shows how to render those values in a campaign.

Hey, did you notice how the template showed your first name?
Your last name is {{.Subscriber.LastName }}.

You have done {{ .Subscriber.Attribs.projects }} projects.


{{ if eq .Subscriber.Attribs.city "Bengaluru" }}
  You live in Bangalore!
{{ else }}
  Where do you live?
{{ end }}


Here is a link for you to click that will be tracked.
<a href="{{ TrackLink "https://google.com" }}">Google</a>

The above example uses an if condition to show one of two messages depending on the value of a subscriber attribute. Many such dynamic expressions are possible with Go templating expressions.

docs.title: System templates
docs.text:
System templates are used for rendering public user-facing pages such as the subscription management page, and in automatically generated system e-mails such as the opt-in confirmation e-mail. These are bundled into listnun but can be customized by copying the static directory locally, and passing its path to listnun with the ./listnun --static-dir=your/custom/path flag.

You can fetch the static files with: mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/listnun/static ; wget -O - https://github.com/nerd-zero/listnun/archive/master.tar.gz | tar xz -C /home/ubuntu/listnun/static --strip=2 "listnun-master/static"

With Docker, mount your copy into the container and pass --static-dir in the command:. Copy the static files from the same version you run, since listnun's public pages differ from listmonk's.

docs.title: Public pages
docs.text:
/static/public/ index.html Base template with the header and footer that all pages use. home.html Landing page on the root domain with the login button. message.html Generic success / failure message page. optin.html Opt-in confirmation page. subscription.html Subscription management page with options for data export and wipe. subscription-form.html List selection and subscription form page.

To edit the appearance of the public pages using CSS and Javascript, head to Settings > Appearance > Public:

docs.title: System e-mails
docs.text:
/static/email-templates/ base.html Base template with the header and footer that all system generated e-mails use. campaign-status.html E-mail notification that is sent to admins on campaign start, completion etc. import-status.html E-mail notification that is sent to admins on finish of an import job. subscriber-data.html E-mail that is sent to subscribers when they request a full dump of their private data. subscriber-optin.html Automatic opt-in confirmation e-mail that is sent to an unconfirmed subscriber when they are added. subscriber-optin-campaign.html E-mail content that's inserted into a campaign body when starting an opt-in campaign from the lists page. default.tpl Default campaign template that is created in Campaigns › Templates when listnun is first installed. This is not used after that.

Info

To turn system e-mail templates to plaintext, remove <!doctype html> from base.html and remove all HTML tags from the templates while retaining the Go templating code.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Warning

Always back up the Postgres database before upgrading.

An upgrade is a new binary plus --upgrade, which brings the database schema up to date. Upgrades are idempotent: running --upgrade again does nothing once the database is current.

docs.title: Binary
docs.text:
1. Build the new version: git pull && make dist. See Installation.
  2. Stop listnun, for example sudo systemctl stop listnun.
  3. Replace the old binary with the new one.
  4. Run ./listnun --upgrade. It runs each pending migration in order and says which.
  5. Start listnun again.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Rebuild the image from the new code, then restart the app container. The container runs --upgrade on start.

git pull && make dist
docker build -t listnun/listnun:latest .
docker compose up -d app

If your docker-compose.yml doesn't run --upgrade in its command:, run it once yourself:

docker compose run --rm app ./listnun --upgrade

docs.title: Upgrading to the redesign (v6.20 to v6.33)
docs.text:
The redesign adds 14 migrations, which --upgrade applies in order. Nothing needs doing by hand, but some behaviour changes:

Migration Change v6.20 Usage metering for billing (usage_counters). v6.21–v6.25 The Developers area: API keys, the transactional message log, transactional templates, email branding and webhooks. v6.26 Deleting a list role no longer deletes the users who had it; they just lose its list access. v6.27 Cloudflare Turnstile and the sign-in captcha setting. v6.28 Media file sizes, for storage reporting. Existing files are measured in the background after the upgrade. v6.29 Each API user becomes an API key. Old username:token pairs keep working until you disable them. See API keys. v6.30 The "require two-step verification" and maximum upload size settings. v6.31 The per-workspace activity log (Settings › Logs). v6.32 Inactive cleanup. It starts off in every workspace. v6.33 Campaign tracking settings. Existing campaigns start with click tracking off, so they send as before. New campaigns have it on.

docs.title: Downgrade
docs.text:
A database upgraded by a newer version shouldn't be used with an older one. To go back:

  1. Stop listnun.
  2. Restore the database backup you took before upgrading.
  3. Run the older binary or image.

docs.title: APIs
docs.text:
All features that are available on the listnun dashboard are also available as REST-like HTTP APIs that can be interacted with directly. Request and response bodies are JSON. This allows easy scripting of listnun and integration with other systems, for instance, synchronisation with external subscriber databases.

Note

If you come across API calls that are yet to be documented, please consider contributing to docs.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: Every workspace has its own address, and API calls go to it: https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/…. The examples on these pages use http://localhost:9000; replace it with your workspace's address.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Authenticate with an API key: its name and secret in the Authorization header.

curl -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…" https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/developers/messages

HTTP Basic auth with the same pair also works:

curl -u "my-service:lnk_live_…" https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/developers/messages

A key belongs to one workspace and only works on that workspace's address.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
A key can only call the endpoints its scopes allow:

Scope Endpoints tx:send POST /api/tx, resending logged messages tx:logs GET /api/developers/messages…, GET /api/developers/stats subscribers:read Reading subscribers (GET /api/subscribers…) keys:manage /api/developers/keys… webhooks:manage /api/developers/webhooks…

The other endpoints on these pages (lists, writing subscribers, imports, campaigns, templates, media, bounces) need a user's permissions, set by their user role and list role. Today they're available to people signed in to the app, and to API users created before API keys existed, which keep working with their username:token pair. New API users can't be created, so new integrations are limited to the key scopes above.

docs.title: Successful request
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "data": {}
}

All responses from the API server are JSON with the content-type application/json unless explicitly stated otherwise. A successful 200 OK response always has a JSON response body with a status key with the value success. The data key contains the full response payload.

docs.title: Failed request
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 500 Server error
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "message": "Error message"
}

A failure response is preceded by the corresponding 40x or 50x HTTP header. There may be an optional data key with additional payload.

docs.title: Timestamps

If provided, replaces the subscriber's current list subscriptions. If omitted, existing subscriptions are kept. attribs JSON JSON object of subscriber attributes. If provided, merged with existing attributes. preconfirm_subscriptions bool If true, subscriptions are marked as confirmed and no opt-in emails are sent for double opt-in lists.

docs.title: API / Transactional
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/tx Send transactional messages

docs.title: POST /api/tx
docs.text: Allows sending transactional messages to one or more subscribers via a preconfigured transactional template.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description subscriber_email string Email of the subscriber. Can substitute with subscriber_id. subscriber_id number Subscriber's ID can substitute with subscriber_email. subscriber_emails string[] Multiple subscriber emails as alternative to subscriber_email. subscriber_ids number[] Multiple subscriber IDs as an alternative to subscriber_id. subscriber_mode string Subscriber lookup mode: default, fallback, or external template_id number Yes ID of the transactional template to be used for the message. from_email string Optional sender email. subject string Optional subject. If empty, the subject defined on the template is used data JSON Optional nested JSON map. Available in the template as {{ .Tx.Data.* }}. headers JSON[] Optional array of email headers. messenger string Messenger to send the message. Default is email. content_type string Email format options include html, markdown, and plain. altbody string Optional alternate plaintext body for multipart HTML emails.

docs.title: Subscriber modes
docs.text:
The subscriber_mode parameter controls how the recipients (subscribers or non-subscriber recipients) are resolved.

Mode Description default Recipients must exist as subscribers in the database. Pass either subscriber_emails or subscriber_ids. fallback Only accepts subscriber_emails and looks up subscribers in the database. If not found, sends the message to the e-mail anyway. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead. external Sends to the given subscriber_emails without subscriber lookup in the database. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_email": "user@test.com",
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"order_id": "1234", "date": "2022-07-30", "items": [1, 2, 3]},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

docs.title: Example response
docs.text:
{
    "data": true
}

docs.title: Example with external mode
docs.text:
Send to arbitrary email addresses without requiring them to be subscribers:

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_mode": "external",
        "subscriber_emails": ["recipient@example.com"],
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"name": "John", "order_id": "1234"},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

In the template, use {{ .Tx.Data.name }}, {{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}, etc. to access the data.

docs.title: File Attachments
docs.text:
To include file attachments in a transactional message, use the multipart/form-data Content-Type. Use data param for the parameters described above as a JSON object. Include any number of attachments via the file param.

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
-F 'data=\"{
    \"subscriber_email\": \"user@test.com\",
    \"template_id\": 4
}"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment.pdf"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment2.pdf"'

docs.title: Developers
docs.text:
The Developers area of the sidebar is for connecting your own systems to listnun: sending transactional email (receipts, password resets, alerts) from your code, and hearing back what happened to it.

Page What it's for Overview A four-step quickstart, plus today's sending numbers and recent messages. API keys Credentials for your code, each limited to the scopes it needs. See API keys. Email templates The transactional templates your code sends. See Transactional email. Send test Send a transactional template from the browser, with sample data, and copy the matching curl command. Message log Every transactional message: who it went to, its status, and the exact payload. Email branding Your logo for transactional emails, including a dark-mode version. See Email branding. Webhooks Endpoints listnun calls when a message is sent, delivered, bounces or fails. See Webhooks.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
1. Create an API key with the tx:send scope under Developers › API keys. Copy the secret. It's shown once.
  2. Pick a transactional template under Developers › Email templates, or create one. Note its ID.

  3. Send a test from your code:

    curl -X POST https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx \
  -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
    "template_id": 3,
    "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"}
  }'

  4. Check the log under Developers › Message log. The message appears within seconds, with a timeline from accepted to delivered or bounced.

docs.title: The rest of the API
docs.text:
Everything you can do in the app can also be done through the REST API: lists, subscribers, campaigns, templates, media, bounces and more. See the API introduction and the reference pages under API.

Template syntax for both campaigns and transactional email is in the Templating reference.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text: An API key lets your code call the listnun API. Create one per service (your shop, your app's backend, a sync job) under Developers › API keys, so you can see where calls come from and revoke one without touching the others.

docs.title: Creating a key
docs.text:
Click Create API key, give it a name, and tick its scopes. Names are 2–63 characters of lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or number, such as shop-backend; the name is also what you authenticate with. listnun shows the secret once; store it in your secrets manager straight away. After that, only its last four characters are shown.

Secrets start with lnk_live_, so they're easy to spot if one leaks into a log or a repository.

Copy your secret now This is the only time it's shown. Store it in your secrets manager. lnk_live_8f2c1d6b0e4a9f37c5b2e8d1a6f0c3b7Copy shop-backendlnk_live_…c3b7tx:sendLast used 2 minutes agoActive crm-synclnk_live_…91aesubscribers:readNot used yetActive old-mailerlnk_live_…07d2tx:sendLast used 3 months agoRevoked

Developers › API keys, just after creating a key.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
A key can only do what its scopes allow. It has no other permissions, whatever its creator can do.

Scope Allows tx:send Sending transactional email (POST /api/tx) and resending logged messages. tx:logs Reading the message log and sending stats. subscribers:read Reading subscribers. keys:manage Listing, creating, rotating and revoking API keys. webhooks:manage Managing webhook endpoints and deliveries.

Give each key the fewest scopes it needs. A service that only sends receipts needs just tx:send.

docs.title: Authenticating
docs.text:
Send the key's name and secret in the Authorization header:

curl https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/developers/messages \
  -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…"

HTTP Basic auth with the same pair also works: curl -u "my-service:lnk_live_…" ….

A key belongs to one workspace and only works on that workspace's address.

docs.title: Rotating
docs.text: Rotate generates a new secret and shows it once. The previous secret keeps working for 24 hours, so you can deploy the new one without downtime. After that, only the new secret works.

docs.title: Revoking and deleting
docs.text:
Revoke stops a key working immediately, but keeps it in the list for your records. Delete removes it completely.

The list shows when each key was last used, which helps you find keys nothing uses any more.

docs.title: Keys migrated from API users
docs.text:
Older workspaces used "API users" (a username and token) instead of keys. Each one has been turned into a key with matching scopes, and its old username:token pair keeps working until you're ready to switch:

  1. Rotate the migrated key to get a real lnk_live_… secret. Until you do, it shows "No key secret yet".
  2. Update your code to use the key's name and new secret.
  3. Choose Disable old token from the key's menu. The old pair stops working.

docs.title: Email branding
docs.text:
Developers › Email branding sets the logo your transactional emails show.

  • Logo: upload or pick an image from your media library.
  • Dark-mode logo (optional): shown by email apps in dark mode. Without one, your logo sits on a white tile in dark mode so it stays readable.
  • Width, alignment and an optional link for the logo.

The preview shows the result in light and dark mode.

docs.title: Using it in templates
docs.text:
Put this where the logo should go in a transactional template:

{{ template "brand-logo" . }}

It renders nothing until a logo is set, so it's safe in every template. To lay the logo out your own way, define your own brand-logo block in the template and it replaces the built-in one.

Campaign templates don't use branding. Put your logo straight into the campaign template's HTML instead.

docs.title: Transactional email
docs.text: A transactional email goes to one person because something happened: an order, a sign-up, a password reset. You send it from your code with POST /api/tx and a transactional template. Unlike a campaign, it isn't sent to a list. By default the recipient must exist as a subscriber in your workspace (on any list or none); set subscriber_mode to fallback or external to send to any address. See the API reference.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Create and edit transactional templates under Developers › Email templates. The editor shows a live preview next to the code, using sample data you can edit.

A transactional template has a subject and a body. Both can use:

  • {{ .Tx.Data.* }}: the data your code sends, e.g. {{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}.
  • {{ .Subscriber.* }}: the recipient, e.g. {{ .Subscriber.Name }}, when they're a subscriber.
  • {{ template "brand-logo" . }}: your workspace logo from Email branding.
{{ template "brand-logo" . }}
<p>Hi {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }},</p>
<p>Thanks for order #{{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}. Your total was {{ .Tx.Data.total }}.</p>

See the Templating reference for everything else you can use.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx \
  -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
    "template_id": 3,
    "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"}
  }'

Your key needs the tx:send scope. The full list of fields (several recipients, sending to people who aren't subscribers, attachments, custom headers) is in the Transactional API reference.

To try a template without writing code, use Developers › Send test: pick the template, enter an address and sample data, and send. It also shows the curl command for the same request.

docs.title: The message log
docs.text:
Developers › Message log lists every transactional message, newest first. Filter by status, template, API key or date, or search by recipient or message ID. Open one to see its timeline and the exact data it was sent with.

Status Meaning queued Accepted, waiting to be sent. sent Handed to the mail server. delivered The receiving mail server accepted it (when your mail provider reports deliveries). bounced It couldn't be delivered. The bounce type is shown. failed listnun couldn't send it, for example because of a template error.

Resend sends a logged message again with the same data. Reading the log needs the tx:logs scope; resending needs tx:send.

To be told about these changes as they happen, set up webhooks.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: A webhook tells your system what happened to a transactional message: listnun sends an HTTP POST to your endpoint each time a message is sent, delivered, bounces or fails. Set them up under Developers › Webhooks.

docs.title: Adding an endpoint
docs.text:
Click Add endpoint, enter its URL, and choose the events it should get. listnun shows the endpoint's signing secret (starting whsec_). Store it; you'll use it to check requests really come from listnun. You can Reveal it again later. Rotate secret replaces it, and deliveries are signed with the new one straight away, so update your endpoint at the same time.

Endpoints must be public https:// addresses. listnun refuses to call private, internal or loopback addresses.

Send test event sends a webhook.test event so you can check your endpoint before real traffic arrives.
